speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are concerned about your infant who has bilious vomiting, abdominal distension, and has not passed meconium. Has your baby had any vomiting since birth, and is the stool completely absent?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's disease.

The clinical picture of bilious vomiting, abdominal distension, and failure to pass meconium in a 2-day-old infant is highly suggestive of a distal intestinal obstruction, most commonly Hirschsprung's disease or meconium ileus. Given the failure to pass meconium within the first 48 hours, I am particularly concerned about Hirschsprung's. I would like to confirm this with an urgent abdominal X-ray and, if possible, an echogenicity scan to visualize the transition zone. Please proceed with REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray and REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray.
